LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.headline: Patriots starter shares positive update after scary knee injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: When speaking with Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller on Monday, Brown explained that the injury was not as bad as initially thought. He even revealed that he was ready to return to practice after missing the team's primetime game against the Chicago Bears last week. Brown's return would be a huge lift for the offense. Van Roten is also eligible to come off injured reserve. So there's at least a chance that the offensive line could start to look much healthier than it has in the last week. Vera-Tucker is expected to return at some point during the season, and the team has not completely closed the door on Onwenu coming back. It sounds like the New England Patriots might have caught a major break with injured offensive lineman Ben Brown. The veteran guard went down with a scary-looking knee injury in the team's Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets. He could barely put weight on his leg when he was helped off the field by the training staff. It was a gut punch to a unit that was already missing Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten. They also lost Alijah Vera-Tucker in the same game. "Availability is of the utmost importance, and so trying to be able to contribute as soon as I can," Brown said. Speaking after Sunday's win, Coach Mike Vrabel was candid about the availability of his banged-up players, especially in an abbreviated week with little downtime available. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Bears are 2nd-best team in the NFC when healthy Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion. home.headline: Patriots at Bears: Injuries, inactives and key matchups for Thursday night’s matchup at Soldier Field
Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears
home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS The Patriots ruled out CB Carlton Davis III (neck), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), G Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring) for Thursday night in Chicago. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. The Pats projected starting offensive line is LT Will Campbell, LG Walter Rouse, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses (questionable) or Caleb Lomu. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. At the skill positions, the Patriots are down two wide receivers, Doubs and Hollins, both on injured reserve. However, the Pats will have top WR A.J. Brown, whose ankle is off the injury report. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. The Patriots could elevate a fifth wide receiver from the practice squad, but that feels unlikely with limited game-day roster spots. Moving over to the defense, starting CB Carlton Davis III (neck) will need to wait at least another week before returning to the lineup. Despite practicing in a limited capacity this week, Davis won't play on Thursday night, marking the third straight game he has missed with his neck injury (four out of the last six). The Patriots held lighter walkthrough sessions during a short week to prepare for the Bears, so Davis may have participated as a ramp-up for a potential return sooner rather than later. The game will be held at the multi-purpose facility in the suburbs of Paris. Pittsburgh was an early 3.5-point favorite on Monday. Things have changed, as the Steelers have been slipped a bit to a 3-point favorite as of Saturday morning. Here are our picks Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 31-17 This is a unpredictable game that could go either way without considering both teams' records. However, the New Orleans Saints' defense does not inspire confidence in stopping the Pittsburgh Steelers. Aaron Rodgers remains a solid quarterback at age 42, passing for nearly 1,500 yards with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Allowing 377 passing yards to Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy does not bode well for New Orleans. While the win over the New York Giants was notable, New York lacked a running back like Jaylen Warren to keep the Saints' defense honest. Warren has rushed for 460 yards on 84 carries, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt. His ability to gain yards after contact, identify lanes and contribute to the passing game gives Pittsburgh multiple offensive options. That creates a difficult matchup for New Orleans. The Saints allows 138 rushing yards per game, ranking 30th in the NFL, while Pittsburgh averages 99.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 20th. Despite Pittsburgh's modest team average, Warren's efficiency indicates the Steelers can exploit the Saints' rushing defense. For New Orleans to win, its offense must perform consistently throughout the game. The Steelers present a tougher matchup than the Giants and have their starting quarterback available. While Tyler Shough offers New Orleans its primary offensive spark, the offensive line must protect him against T.J. Watt, who excels at pressuring quarterbacks. Pittsburgh also features a stronger pass rush and secondary than New York. Steelers 31 Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 28-21 After getting their collective tails chewed out by the team owner a week and a half ago, the Saints put together a better effort in a win at the New York Football Giants last weekend. Now, after a week in the mother country (at least the one for New Orleans and its state), players and coaches alike are saying this is the best week of practice the team has had all season. Meanwhile, a visibly exhausted Aaron Rodgers spoke to the media on Thursday, the day his Pittsburgh Steelers arrived in Paris, worried about jet lag and getting to France so late in the week. True, the Steelers are favored, and rightfully so with a flip-flop record of 4-2 compared to the Saints. But this game seems more and more like a home game for New Orleans fans as even Harry's New York Bar "changed its name" for one day to celebrate the team and its fans. Harry's New York Bar becomes Harry's New Orleans Bar for one day. | Harry's New York Bar Instagram There is, of course, the immediate retort that home field advantage is a myth for this program. And if you thought that, you'd be correct, as the Saints haven't won at home since December 21, 2025. However, most of us didn't see the turnaround this team did in a week. Add to that, the team's ability to acclimate to a different time zone, and Pittsburgh's lack thereof, and I see a Saints victory. Pittsburgh has playoff expectations in the 2026 season, and new head coach Mike McCarthy has his team at a 4-2 start through six weeks. However, the AFC North has four teams over .500, putting the Steelers in a spot where they can't afford many losses early in the season. Meanwhile, New Orleans is off to a 2-4 start, snapping a three-game skid in Week 6 when they beat the New York Giants. Shough and company have performed pretty well on offense, but New Orleans is sitting in third place in the division at just 2-4 through the first six weeks. This is technically a home game for the Saints, and they're set as underdogs against Rodgers and the Steelers. This line opened up 2.5 points (Pittsburgh favored), and it has since moved to three. The Steelers have a top-10 defense in EPA/Play, while the Saints are a bottom-10 unit and sit dead last in the league in EPA/Rush. That could offer some interesting prop spots with the Steelers' backfield of Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren looking pretty strong in their Week 6 win against Tampa Bay. So, how should bettors wager on the NFL’s first-ever game in France? All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections and a few anytime touchdown scorer choices for this game in Paris. So, why not put all of our favorites in one spot? This column is a one-stop shop for the NFL Paris matchup to get bettors ready for the first game in Sunday’s 12-game slate. He’s backing Pittsburgh to cover the spread in Paris as a “road” favorite: The Steelers' run game against the Saints' run defense will be the biggest difference-maker in this game. Pittsburgh has done a great job running the football this season, ranking fifth in rush EPA, and Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry. Now they face a Saints defense that's last in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, while also giving up 4.8 yards per rush. If Warren can be effective on the ground, the Saints' offense will struggle to keep pace. The Steelers' defense is top 10 in the NFL in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. Let's hope that defense travels. I'm going to back the Steelers as favorites in France. Saints wide receiver Chris Olave has two touchdowns in the 2026 season, and he’s actually seen his targets drop (13 total in the last two weeks) after four straight double-digit target games to open the season. Despite that, I’m buying low on the former Ohio State star on Sunday. The Steelers have allowed just six passing scores this season and are sixth in the league in EPA/Pass, but Olave has been the focal point of this Saints team that throws the ball almost as much as anyone in the NFL. The Saints are third in the league in pass attempts in 2026, and Olave has drawn 61 looks in six games. There are other options to consider for the Saints (Devaughn Vele, Juwan Johnson), but I’ll gladly take a true No. 1 receiver at nearly 2/1 to find the end zone in Week 7. The Saints have been awful against the run this season, ranking dead last in the NFL in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.8 yards per carry. That’s a great sign for Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren, who is averaging 5.5 yards per carry and already has 460 rushing yards in six games this season. Even with Rico Dowdle (toe) returning to action in Week 6, Warren led the backfield by playing over 74 percent of the snaps and handling 14 carries. He finished the day with 50 rushing yards and 28 receiving yards. While this prop is a little higher than that, Warren had a three-game streak with 90 or more rushing yards snapped in Week 6. Tampa Bay is third in the NFL in EPA/Rush this season, so this is a much easier matchup for Warren in Week 7. He’s handled at least 10 carries in every game, including 14 or more in four straight. Since the veteran has taken the clear lead in this backfield, I expect him to be the biggest beneficiary against this Saints defense. Rookie receiver Germie Bernand has been forced into a bigger role with Pittsburgh's injuries this season, and he’s thriving in it. The second-round pick had nine targets and six catches in Week 5 against Indianapolis, and he followed that up with a massive day in the win against Tampa Bay. Bernard found the end zone for the first time in his career, and he caught 11 of his 12 looks from Rodgers for 87 yards. Since Rodgers isn’t really pushing the ball down the field, I love this receptions prop for Bernand, as he’s emerged as the No. 2 receiver behind DK Metcalf. The rookie played over 91 percent of the snaps in each of the last two weeks, and he’s clearly established a solid rapport with Rodgers. I think he’s a great target against a Saints defense that is in the bottom 10 in the league in EPA/Pass, opponent completions and opponent passing yards in 2026. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Saints Bold Predictions: Offense Puts on a Show Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Pittsburgh Steelers are officially in France and are ready to take on the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris. Riding a two-game win streak heading into Week 7, the Steelers still have things to clean up as they look to keep pace in the race for both the AFC North and one of three Wild Card spots in the conference. Regardless, Pittsburgh is 4-2 for a fourth-straight season and has what some may consider a must-win type of game vs. New Orleans given how tough its schedule gets immediately following its Week 9 bye. With that, here are three bold predictions for the Steelers as they look to take down the Saints. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Pittsburgh's offense largely falls near the middle of the pack, averaging the 12th-fewest yards (320.5) and the 15th-fewest points (22.8) per game in the league. Those numbers are dragged down quite a bit by the team's poor outing against the New England Patriots in Week 2, however, during which they scored just three points with 235 yards of offense. Under Mike McCarthy, the Steelers have proven that they're at least capable of explosive offensive performances. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance. New Orleans' defense is currently tied with the Arizona Cardinals for the most points allowed per game (29.7) while also giving up the fourth-most yards per contest (377.7). The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3) and Pittsburgh Steelers safety Robert Spears-Jennings (28) celebrate after a play during the fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Win by Two Scores Steelers Win by Two Scores Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. The league heads to Paris for Week 7 of the 2026 season where Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the New Orleans Saints and second-year signal-caller Tyler Shough. Pittsburgh is right back in the playoff mix in the AFC this season, sitting at 4-2 through six weeks after a comeback win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6. It hasn't always been pretty for the Steelers this season, but their defense (sixth in EPA/Play) has been one of the best in the league, helping them stay in games. Rodgers ranks just 30th amongst quarterbacks with at least 50 plays this season in success rate, which is a bit of a concern against a New Orleans team that has been able to put points on the board this season. The Saints’ defense is just 27th in EPA/Play, but Shough has moved the ball pretty well in his second NFL season, leading New Orleans to a win over the New York Giants last Sunday. Oddsmakers have set the Steelers as “road” favorites in this matchup, and they need every win they can get with the AFC North featuring four over .500 teams through the first six weeks. All season long, the SI Betting team has shared our final score predictions for every NFL game, and with the league exploring the Paris market, we’re still here to give picks. The fun part of these final score predictions is that they are intended to give bettors some insight on how to bet on the spread, moneyline and total each week. With Pittsburgh in the thick of a playoff race and New Orleans looking to get back in the NFC South mix, who wins in Paris? Let’s check out the latest odds, analysis and my score prediction for the first matchup in the NFL on Sunday. Pittsburgh is now favored by 3.5 – a whole point move – and is -185 on the moneyline to get the win. A 5-2 start would put Aaron Rodgers and company in a great spot to make the playoffs in the AFC, though all four teams in the division are over .500 through six weeks. Steelers vs. Saints Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . He’s backing Pittsburgh to cover the spread in Paris as it looks to move to 5-2: The Steelers' run game against the Saints' run defense will be the biggest difference-maker in this game. Pittsburgh has done a great job running the football this season, ranking fifth in rush EPA, and Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry. Now they face a Saints defense that's last in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, while also giving up 4.8 yards per rush. If Warren can be effective on the ground, the Saints' offense will struggle to keep pace. The Steelers' defense is top 10 in the NFL in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. Let's hope that defense travels. I'm going to back the Steelers as favorites in France. I love MacMillan’s reasoning for this bet, and I’m also taking the Steelers to win on Sunday morning. Shough has put up some big passing stats in games this season, but he’s still just 20th in success rate amongst QBs with at least 50 plays in the 2026 campaign. This New Orleans team also has one good win (over Baltimore) and some questionable losses through six weeks. The defense is one of the worst in the NFL, and Week 6 showed that Pittsburgh’s defense can take over a game, especially against a young quarterback. The Steelers shut down Tampa Bay in the second half and ended up winning in overtime despite Rodgers and the offense struggling most of the day. I don’t expect a ton of points from Pittsburgh – that simply hasn’t been the team's M.O. in 2026 – but it should do enough to cover in Week 7. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

Atlanta is searching for its first home win of the season, but San Francisco presents a major test for a team still trying to find consistency on both sides of the ball. Despite the 49ers dealing with injuries, the Falcons will need a complete performance to pull off the upset. Here is how our staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Garrett Chapman (3-3) The Falcons are winless at home this season, and they will need to pass a difficult test Sunday to change that trend. The undefeated 49ers have established themselves as one of the league’s top teams, and Atlanta enters the matchup with defensive holes to fill and an offense still searching for consistency. If Michael Penix Jr. can stay clean in the pocket, the Falcons will have a legitimate chance to compete. However, slowing down George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be especially difficult without linebacker Divine Deablo. San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17 Scott Kennedy (3-3): At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated. The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages. San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult. Prediction : 49ers 31, Falcons 23 Darius Hayes (3-3): After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory. San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback. I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump. San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss. This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however. The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. picks.headline: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert
picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. away.headline: 49ers week 7 injury report is bad news for WR Mike Evans
away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. After being listed as questionable on the injury report, Stout is officially active against Atlanta. Safety Siran Neal is also up after receiving a 'questionable' designation. San Francisco on Saturday announced its Week 7 roster moves. Those moves included officially activating Kirk off IR where he's been since final cuts. He practiced in Week 6, but didn't play. He was a full go in practice by the end of Week 7 which cleared the way for him to return just in time to step in for Evans. 49ers Week 7 injury report: Mike Evans among 6 ruled out It's not a surprise Evans is out while he deals with Achilles tendinitis, but Shanahan used the same language about the injury for Week 7 that he did leading up to Week 6 when Evans suited up despite not practicing. After Evans left Week 6 late in the first half and with the bye week lingering it behooves the 49ers to shut the 33-year-old receiver down. This will be the first game Evans misses with the 49ers. Christian Kirk trending toward return in Week 7 It's not a huge surprise to see optimism about Kirk's return for the 49ers' game in Atlanta. With Mike Evans potentially out because of Achilles tendinitis San Francisco needs reinforcements. Kirk's practice window was opened before Week 6, and now with a second week of practice in it sounds like the club is gearing up for him to come back in Week 7. Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Thursday spoke with KNBR and said Kirk is trending toward making his 2026 debut. " He looked good out there ," Shanahan said. "Talking to him he felt good, and I think he felt good last week. So it's trending in the right direction." The 49ers only open the first portion of practice to media, and neither Bosa nor Evans were on hand for the open part of the session according to reporters on site. Evans is working through Achilles tendonitis. He didn't practice leading up to Week 6 and still suited up before exiting the game late in the second quarter. For Bosa there was optimism he'd be back Thursday. Early indications are he isn't going to participate, but that could change if he comes out after media exit. Kyle Shanahan hopes Nick Bosa will return to practice Thursday Bosa has been out since Week 3 when he suffered a calf injury. The issue wasn't supposed be long-term and there was some hope he'd return for Week 6. Bosa didn't practice at all in Week 6 before being ruled out. He didn't participate in Wednesday's session, but head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed some optimism the star defensive end would be in the team's second practice of the week. "Can't go today, but hoping he'll be out there tomorrow," Shanahan said before practice. There may not be a team in the NFL more in need of a Bye week than the San Francisco 49ers . away.headline: 49ers Week 7 injury report vs. Falcons: Who will step up for SF with Mike Evans potentially out
away.blurb: Evans has been ruled out with Achilles, rib injuries He has been battling Achilles tendinitis this season. He left the Week 6 victory over the Commanders at halftime, and he has been ruled out of this game . In addition to the Achilles issue, Evans has a rib injury that is also impacting him. The hope for the 49ers is that he will be able to return in Week 9 when the Niners host the Las Vegas Raiders. Samuel is also out for the Niners Making matters worse for the 49ers is that fellow wideout Deebo Samuel will also miss the game. He is the team’s second-leading wide receiver, and he has a hamstring issue that is clearly impacting his ability to move on the football field. He was not able to participate in practice at any point this week and Shanahan also ruled him out of the game. McCaffrey is far more than a safety valve receiver out of the backfield. He can run multiple short, medium and long routes, and the Niners will likely use him out of the backfield in that fashion in this game. In addition to Evans and Samuel, edge rusher Nick Bosa has been ruled out with a calf injury. Other notable players who have been ruled out include starting S Marques Sigle with an ankle injury and depth LB Grant Wallow with a hamstring problem. This is not a must game for the 49ers. Their 6-0 record has given them a three-game lead over the Seattle Seahawks, and the most important thing for the Niners will be coming out of this game without any additional injuries. That may not be something they can control, but it is clearly something that could matter more than remaining undefeated at this point in the season. Related: 49ers’ Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel already ruled out for Falcons showdown The San Francisco 49ers have been brilliant to this point in the season and they have managed an undefeated record (6-0) as they prepare for their final game before the bye week. They are facing an inconsistent Atlanta Falcons team that is going to be determined to bounce back from a 31-23 defeat to the Chicago Bears. The circumstances of the game are also tough for the 49ers , because they are coming off a surprisingly tight 23-17 Monday night victory over the Washington Commanders, so that means they have are contending with a short week to prepare for a somewhat dangerous opponent. Head coach Kyle Shanahan will not concede anything in this game because he has one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Brock Purdy and he has been sensational to this point in the season. The same holds for running back Christian McCaffrey. Purdy has been on fire for the Niners It will be very difficult for the Falcons to slow either one down. Purdy is already in the discussion for the Most Valuable Player Award as he has completed 119 of 171 passes for 1,460 yards with 14 touchdown passes and 2 interceptions. The San Francisco offensive line has protected him quite well, as Purdy has been sacked just 5 times. McCaffrey may no longer be as quick or as explosive as he was during his peak years

away.headline: 49ers Injury Report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have 48 available players against Falcons
away.blurb: 49ers injury report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have enough available players to reach 48 for Week 7 vs. Falcons. Shanahan said he did not think he had ever faced a situation like this in his coaching career, calling it a unique situation. For a team trying to stay unbeaten on the trip to Atlanta, the concern is not just who will be unavailable, but whether the 49ers can even fill out a full game-day roster. Which players are out for Week 7? According to Shanahan, Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Marques Sigle, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford were unavailable or ruled out on Sunday. Christian Kirk was in line to make his season debut, but the overall health picture still left the roster in a difficult spot. The Bosa situation was particularly notable because Shanahan said the pass rusher had worked out after previously saying he might be able to return for Week 5 or Week 6. Shanahan said Bosa was a little sore the next day, which surprised the team and did not help the outlook for this week, especially with turf coming into play. Being short on available players is one thing. Being short enough to potentially miss the 48-man threshold is another. NFL teams can elevate players from the practice squad when injuries create depth problems, and that kind of move could become important for the 49ers if the injury list keeps growing. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. picks.headline: Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans: Week 7 Predictions
picks.blurb: Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans: Week 7 Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans: Week 7 Predictions Spencer German Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads At 4-2 and in first place in the AFC North, the Cleveland Browns are starting to really earn some respect across the NFL, but a loss to the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 would erase some of that good will they've built up in recent weeks. Aside from their records, these two teams are oddly similar. Their defenses tend to carry them and keep games close, while their offenses tend to struggle, particularly early on in games. Cleveland is well-equipped to win those slog-style games, but will they slip up in the Music City? Here are our predictions for Week 7. Anthony Moeglin It's a Cleveland Browns party on Broadway this weekend in Nashville, Tennessee. The Browns come into this game as the favorite for the first time all season and probably the last time all season. They have a chance to get to 5-2 on the year and stay in first place. They get it done on Sunday against the Titans. Spencer German Last week was a barometer game to assess how the Browns stack up with a legitimate Super Bowl contender, even if that contender was missing it's MVP quarterback. But this week, in some ways is an even bigger test of whether or not the Browns are as good as their record says they are. Great teams beat the teams they're supposed to beat and Cleveland does just that on Sunday to improve to 5-2. Yes, it is basically a Pick 'Em heading into Sunday. Cleveland is -1.5 favorites in this one, and I see a 20-3 winner for Cleveland where the defense shuts it down, and the offense gets it going a little bit on Sunday. This one is basically a Pick 'em with the Browns being listed as favorites for the first time this season (and on the road nonetheless) by 1.5. I think that means they easily cover, with a 17-9 victory. A 300-yard day for Deshaun Watson I'm 0-6 on bold predictions this year, so let's go way out there. Deshaun Watson throws for 300 yards on Sunday for the first time in his Cleveland Browns career. It would be a monumental day down in Tennessee if this bold prediction comes true. The Browns score 7 on their opening drive Despite Todd Monken's presence as an elite offensive mind, the Browns have yet to score on an opening drive this season. They've also only scored six points in the first quarter this season. In a game featuring two struggling offenses, the one that gets off to a better start could be in the driver's seat for a win. Finally, Cleveland gets to play with a lead.

away.headline: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. home.headline: Browns Week 7 Injury Report Brings Mostly Good News for Titans Matchup
home.blurb: Ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans , only two active players were officially ruled out for Cleveland in defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. and guard Teven Jenkins. Two others, DT Kalia Davis, as well as quarterback Dillon Gabriel were ruled out as well, but both remain on the IR for now. Meanwhile, a pretty star-heavy list of four players are listed as questionable for Sunday, starting with Grant Delpit, who has been in concussion protocol this week after exiting Sunday's win over the Ravens six plays into action with a head injury. He's been limited at practice in recent days as he works his way through the league's protocol. Running back Dillon Sampson is another, as is looking to return off the IR after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. He was limited throughout week, but could be activated to the active roster on Saturday and suit up on Sunday. Linebacker Quincy Williams was a late addition to the injury report this week after suffering a neck injury. He missed practice on Thursday, returned on Friday, but will still head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Similarly, cornerback Denzel Ward popped up on Friday's report with a hand injury and was limited at practice, promoting a questionable designation for him, as well. However, they do not match up well with the Minnesota Vikings this Sunday. The Indianapolis Colts (2-4) will attempt to ground themselves on Sunday as they travel to Minneapolis to face the host Minnesota Vikings (5-0) before their season truly spirals out of control. The Colts' 2026 campaign is at a crossroads. After consecutive losses, including an embarrassing finish last week to the previously winless Tennessee Titans , the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . Will that move spark the Colts and help them turn the tide, or will the team retreat into its shell? Trade rumors and thoughts of a slide are once again surrounding the Colts. This game could be a back-breaker unless they can avoid it. Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Vikings 23, Colts 13 "I'd often like to lead with the optimistic take on the matchup with a clear advantage the Colts have over their opponent, but I'm not sure there is one this week. Minnesota's defense blitzes far more than any other team, which is something the Colts' offense struggles against. The Colts can usually run the ball, but opponents are running against Minnesota less than anyone else because of the defensive fronts the Vikings present. The Vikings' offense isn't doing well despite having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson, but they've had a week to figure out what to do, coming off their bye. "The Colts would often have the edge on special teams and penalties, but Minnesota's special teams are just as good as Indy's, if not better, and the Colts and Vikings are tied for being the second-least-penalized teams in the NFL. picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs.
