The Dolphins have arrived at one of the games circled on the calendar as presenting one of the team's best opportunities to win in this rebuilding season, though the national consensus remains overwhelmingly in favor of a loss. At least there's some movement forward after three weeks of unanimous predictions of a loss, followed by one single media member predicting a Miami win in its last game against Cincinnati in Week 5. As we said, the Dolphins still are widely expected to lose, but there is some progress in terms of their predictions, however small. away.blurb: Miami (1-5) used a ground-control offense - and a pair of TD passes from Malik Willis to Caleb Douglas - to pull off the upset of New York (2-5). Douglas returned from an ankle injury that had kept him out for the last three games. He only caught two passes - but he made them count. Dolphins veteran center Aaron Brewer says coach Jeff Hafley showed trust in the offensive line late in the game when Miami was trying to run out the clock and keep the ball away from the surging Jets. EDGE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring) was listed as doubtful, while LB Willie Gay Jr. (illness) and S Kyle Louis (knee) are questionable. QB Malik Willis was a full participant at practice all week despite a right thumb injury , while RB Jaylen Wright (foot) bumped up to full practice Friday. For the Jets, LB Francisco Mauigoa (quad), DE Joseph Ossai (ankle) and OT Max Mitchell (concussion) were listed as out, while RBs Breece Hall (quad) and Kene Nwangwu (knee) and G Dylan Parham (knee) were questionable. The Jets rallied in the second half but came up short. The key play was a QB sneak by Willis at midfield with just under 2:00 to play. Willis had his best game in a Dolphin uniform, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards with the 2 TD passes for a 130.7 QB rating. Ollie Gordon led the ground game with 103 yards on 25 carries and one TD. It has led to a solid running game and, on Sunday, a defeat of the New York Jets. Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas scored two touchdowns in a 28-25 victory at the Jets. He had missed the last three games after spraining his ankle in a Week 2 loss at the San Francisco 49ers. It was his first two professional touchdowns - and they were his only receptions on the day. home.blurb: Miami (1-5) used a ground-control offense - and a pair of TD passes from Malik Willis to Caleb Douglas - to pull off the upset of New York (2-5). Douglas returned from an ankle injury that had kept him out for the last three games. He only caught two passes - but he made them count. Dolphins veteran center Aaron Brewer says coach Jeff Hafley showed trust in the offensive line late in the game when Miami was trying to run out the clock and keep the ball away from the surging Jets. Joe Schad: Ollie Gordon for 14 ... Ollie Gordon for 7 ... Ollie Gordon over 100 yards rushing. Dolphins trying to smash their way out of Jersey with a win It's 28-25 Miami with 2:00 left. There is a near 0% chance of rain. CB Reese Taylor is out with a quad injury. EDGE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring) was listed as doubtful, while LB Willie Gay Jr. (illness) and S Kyle Louis (knee) are questionable. The Jets rallied in the second half but came up short. The key play was a QB sneak by Willis at midfield with just under 2:00 to play. It was his first two professional touchdowns - and they were his only receptions on the day. With the NFL season nearly halfway complete, a number of coaches are on hot-seat watch. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn could be one to watch in the coming weeks. "Nothing hard and fast right now as far as his tenure, from what I'm hearing after asking around," Fowler said (1:00 mark). "Look, Woody Johnson, the owner there, is really happy with Aaron Glenn as a whole as far as the progress they made in the offseason from Year 1 to Year 2... But that is a job to watch now, cause in Year 2, they're still struggling with some clock management issues." Amid the Indianapolis Colts' struggles, Fowler also pointed to Shane Steichen as another coach who could be on the hotseat. "Shane Steichen could be a lame duck situation at this point," Fowler said. "Now, they do value him. They want to give him a little bit of time. Talking to people around the league, they suspected that this window of time, dating back to the Minnesota game yesterday, the Jaguars game coming up and that next week before the trade deadline. If they can sort of get right and win at least one or two games, it could change their plan for their coaches and what they sell." They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup. The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 21 It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around. Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back. While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points. I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again. James Hill, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 20 Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury. Collin Haalboom, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 17 The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan. So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not. Logan Robinson, Founder: Panthers 28, Bucs 23 The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season. My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team. River Wells, Editor: Panthers 28, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points. Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning. Consensus: Panthers 5, Bucs 0 The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning. Meanwhile, Cincy is coming out of a bye week and is in a prime spot to make a run up the AFC North standings. After this game, the Bengals take on Tennessee, Atlanta, Pittsburgh, Washington and New Orleans (four teams under .500) to close out October and November. After missing the playoffs last season, Cincy is hoping a healthy Burrow is enough to make a playoff run in 2026. With Lamar Jackson officially ruled out due to an ankle injury, my Bengals vs. Ravens prediction backs Cincinnati to capitalize in today's pivotal AFC North showdown. Fresh off their bye week, the Bengals head to M&T Bank Stadium as 1.5-point road favorites, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Baltimore's quarterback situation opens the door for some intriguing trading opportunities, and my latest NFL picks target value across the moneyline, anytime touchdown, and completions markets this afternoon. TOP Pick Bengals vs Ravens prediction today: Bengals moneyline Editor's note: Jackson has now officially been ruled out and will miss his third straight game. Even though I gave them out at +2.5 earlier this week , I'm still willing to trade the Cincinnati Bengals 51% moneyline, up to 53% , against the Baltimore Ravens . Lamar Jackson has been limited in practice all week after missing the past two games, so there is no way he'll be 100% Sunday if he plays at all. An injured Lamar weakens Baltimore's offense , especially its ground game, because he's less likely to run, which is his biggest skill. Jackson averaged only 20.1 rushing yards per game when he returned from injury last season, and the Ravens missed the playoffs. Meanwhile, Cincinnati enters off a bye with a much cleaner injury situation . Since 2024, Baltimore is 1-5 against the spread (ATS) with a rest disadvantage and a -4.8 spread differential. For a straight-up pick on every game, see our NFL moneyline picks for Week 7 . Bengals vs Ravens combo This combo makes sense if Cincinnati turns the game into a Joe Burrow -controlled grind instead of asking its rushing attack to carry the offense. I want the Bengals living in manageable down-and-distance situations, stacking first downs, and forcing Baltimore to defend long possessions. That naturally gives Burrow more chances to pile up completions while increasing the odds that Ja'Marr Chase eventually finishes one of those drives in the end zone. The other side of the script matters, too. If Baltimore's offense is less explosive than usual, Cincinnati can stay patient and keep leaning on what Burrow does best. Give me Burrow moving the chains, Chase cashing in near the goal line, and the Bengals hanging around long enough to finish the job. Cincinnati may have to lean more heavily on Burrow's arm in this matchup. The Bengals rank 27th in yards per rush, while Baltimore is ninth in yards per rush allowed, making the passing game the cleaner path to points. And if Burrow is throwing near the goal line, Chase is obviously his first look. Chase has eight touchdowns in 10 career games against Baltimore and leads Cincinnati with four touchdown catches this season. Some receivers can be schemed out of games. Chase usually isn't one of them. For more touchdown props, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks for Week 7 . Burrow owns the highest completion rate in NFL history at 68.6% and is completing a league-high 71.4% of his passes this season. He's also been dinking and dunking more, ranking 24th in intended air yards per attempt . That style fits this prop perfectly. Burrow has completed 25+ passes in three of five games this season and averages 25.4 completions in 11 career meetings with Baltimore , clearing 25+ in six of them. Want more NFL player props? They currently sit at the bottom of the AFC North with a 3-2 record. The 4-2 Ravens are coming off a 13-10 loss to Cleveland. Joe Burrow did not mince words about avoiding a 0-2 division record: "We want to be 4-2 and controlling our own destiny." Baltimore has taken five of the last six meetings in this rivalry, including a 24-0 shutout last winter. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Dexter Lawrence Sacks the Quarterback Twice Cincinnati brought in All-Pro tackle Dexter Lawrence to make life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Lawrence shares the team sack lead with three, anchoring a defensive front that brings down passers on 10.12% of attempts. Baltimore's reshuffled offensive line gives him another opportunity to take over. Cam Jurgens is set to make his Ravens debut at center after recovering from a concussion, pushing Vega Ioane over to right guard. That leaves Jurgens with a difficult first assignment against Cincinnati's 340-pound anchor. Lawrence will dominate the A-gap, dropping Baltimore's signal-caller twice and collapsing the pocket before deep plays can develop. Tee Higgins Explodes for Over 100 Yards and Two Touchdowns Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) and wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) celebrate a Higgins touchdown in the second quarter of the NFL Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. The game was tied at 17 at halftime. Baltimore's secondary will have its hands full matching up on the perimeter. Ja'Marr Chase usually attracts plenty of attention from opposing defenses. That could leave Tee Higgins with more opportunities to exploit one-on-one coverage on the outside. Zac Taylor called Higgins a "major weapon" outside, pointing out that his past production against Baltimore often gets overlooked. Baltimore loves flooding the field with six defensive backs, but smaller defensive backs cannot match Higgins' massive frame . Burrow is going to test those 50-50 balls down the sideline, letting Higgins sprint his way to 100 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Jordan Battle Jumps a Route for Another Takeaway Jordan Battle is playing like a ball-hawking magnet right now. He shares the NFL lead with three interceptions after picking off two passes in Miami , and Taylor said this week that "turnovers scream at you" in division dogfights. Baltimore's passing attack has hit dead ends late in games, going scoreless in the second half three times. Backup Tyler Huntley averages just six yards a pop, while Lamar Jackson is working through a sore ankle. Battle will bait a throw over the middle, jump the passing lane, and flip the field with another huge takeaway. Boye Mafe and the Front Stop Derrick Henry Under 60 Yards Derrick Henry leads the league in rushing scores, but Cincinnati's rebuilt front is ready for the challenge. Taylor praised Mafe's work against the run earlier this week, saying that the defensive end's "willingness to set an edge and win in the run game is equally as critical as being able to rush the passer." Mafe and Cincinnati's front will swarm the boundary on early downs. By stacking the box and sealing outside lanes, Cincinnati will limit Henry to under 60 yards. away.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. The 10-year veteran appeared in six games for the Steelers this season, made one start, and recorded 15 tackles. Pittsburgh’s release announcement credited him with 145 career appearances, 93 starts, and 11 interceptions. Baltimore needs depth immediately with starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins sidelined by a knee injury. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. picks.blurb: Texans' Week 7 Odds Point to Potential Blowout vs. Giants, J.J. McCarthy Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Houston Texans head into their Week 7 contest against the New York Giants riding the high of logging two straight wins over their last two matchups, and now hope to extend that streak to three in their last game before the bye. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.blurb: In Week 7, the New York Giants faced off against the Houston Texans . While they came into the game at 2-4, the Texans were not an easy opponent. But the Giants took it to overtime, where they came out on top. Skattebo might've been in jeopardy of missing Week 8, but the team is on a bye, and this report indicates that he should be good to go for the team's Week 9 matchup coming out of the bye when they face the Philadelphia Eagles . away.headline: Report: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo avoided major injury
away.blurb: The extra rest should allow Skattebo to return healthy to the backfield as New York aims to maintain its divisional edge. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo should avoid significant injury after feeling something in his hamstring on a 42-yard overtime run that helped secure a 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported on Monday that all indications are the second-year back should be OK, a rare positive for a Giants team that often has injured reserve (IR) candidates after games, particularly with a bye this weekend. After the Week 7 win, Skattebo told ESPN’s Dan Graziano he did not intend to slide on the play that set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning 30-yard touchdown. He felt something in his hamstring and knew the Giants were in field-goal range, so he went down at the Houston 30. He noted the bye week’s timing was fortunate. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reported that Skattebo avoided straining the muscle. The carry was the longest of Skattebo’s career and highlighted a bounce-back outing in which he rushed 17 times for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown. It followed a week in which he received zero carries against the New Orleans Saints after an overtime fumble versus the Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Giants improved to 4-2-1, leading the NFC East, and will have the bye before traveling to Philadelphia on November 8. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL J-Dub suffers devastating injury New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. "This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. Things won't get much easier for them in Week 7 when they host the Denver Broncos, who are 4-2 on the year. You can find my best bet for this game in this week's edition of the Road to 272 Bets. In this article, you'll find my favorite prop bets. Let's dive into them. Broncos vs. Cardinals Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via BetMGM Sportsbook Bo Nix OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (+115) Michael Wilson OVER 4.5 Receptions (-115) Jaylen Waddle Anytime Touchdown (+200) In this week's edition of the Player Prop Countdown , I broke down why Bo Nix to throw for 2+ touchdowns is my favorite prop of Week 7: I understand the Bo Nix narrative heading into this week, but we have to cut him a little bit of slack. He has had to face a murderers' row of defenses this season, including the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, and Seahawks. He now gets to face by far the easiest defense he's faced this season. The Cardinals rank 30th in opponent dropback EPA, 25th in opponent dropback success rate, and they've allowed 16 passing touchdowns, the most in the NFL. At plus-money, I'll jump all over him to throw for at least two scores on Sunday. Michael Wilson has been having an underrated season thus far. Not only is he already averaging over five receptions per game, but now with Marvin Harrison Jr. in Houston, he should get even more looks as the team's primary target at wide receiver. If the Broncos take an early lead, the Cardinals will have to go to the air even more, giving Wilson plenty of opportunities to haul in 5+ receptions. Jaylen Waddle has nine more receptions than any other wide receiver on the Denver Broncos, and now he gets to face a Cardinals' defense that's in the bottom 10 in virtually every single pass defense metric. That could lead to big things for Waddle, who is due for another touchdown after having scored just one through his first six games as a Bronco. He's a great bet to score on Sunday at 2-1 odds. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. After sitting out Sunday's game, Pat Surtain told the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson that he wasn't really close to playing in Week 7. When asked if he could return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, Surtain said, "Possibly." Broncos CB Pat Surtain is inactive and will miss his third straight game. However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport tweeted on Sunday that " there's a good chance " Surtain will be able to return against the Chiefs in Week 8. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. away.headline: Broncos’ Jaylen Waddle injured chest on ‘dumb’ Sean Payton play call: ‘It was awful’
away.blurb: When he rolled over, Waddle grabbed his left chest and shoulder area with his right hand and didn't get up until trainers came out to check on him. The team ultimately called it a chest injury. Is Jonah Coleman Broncos' RB1? Rookie's return sparks Denver's ground game against Cardinals Waddle was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday with what was listed as a chest injury, then was a full participant Friday and was cleared to play against the Cardinals. Allen finished a play on Arizona's final drive, then grabbed his right hamstring and sat down. Trainers came out to look at him and he eventually walked off gingerly on his own. That development wasn't a huge surprise after Surtain was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report. Since he was first injured against San Francisco in early October, the Broncos have been aiming for a Week 8 return for Surtain. That's next weekend against Kansas City. Denver second-year defensive lineman Sai'Vion Jones has carved out a nice role for himself as a sophomore in the NFL. Jones, a 2025 third-round pick out of LSU, sacked Arizona's Jacoby Brissett early in the fourth quarter. It helped the Broncos defense get to its feet, too, after a 27-yard completion to star tight end Trey McBride (10 catches, 111 yards, TD). Denver followed up Jones' sack by forcing a turnover on downs. Branded Content Advertising by Ascend 7 Thoughts after Broncos beat Cards Waddle grabbed at his left chest area after recovering a fumble on a botched reverse GLENDALE, Ariz — Sean Payton took matters into his own hands. Five minutes into his postgame news conference after a 30-16 win over Arizona , the Broncos head coach called his own number — and criticized himself in the process. “Why hasn't anyone asked me about the dumb reverse call?” Payton wondered, getting more animated as he talked. “I'm going to answer. Everyone ask the question. “It was awful, alright, I'm sorry.” Payton had a historical comparison, too. “If you look it up, in 2008 in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse,” he said. “Fumbled. Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play.” Arizona didn't come back and beat the Broncos, of course, but the play did lose 11 yards. Denver retained possession because top wide receiver Jaylen Waddle fell on the ball. The problem this time around? Waddle also got hurt on the play . It came with 4:51 left in regulation and Denver leading by two touchdowns. Payton, who felt he and the offensive staff had put together a terrific game plan against Arizona's zone-blitzing defense, dialed up a reverse for his top receiver. The ball got fumbled, though, and Waddle jumped on it. After stopping in the medical tent for evaluation, Waddle left the game and headed back to the locker room. Surtain was a limited participant in all three practices this week, and the Broncos listed him as questionable on Friday's final injury report. Surtain, who has missed Denver's last two games with an ankle injury, is unlikely to play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The update comes after Surtain returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering a non-contact ankle injury during Denver's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 4. The injury initially raised significant concerns because Surtain went down without contact late in the first half against San Francisco. However, the Broncos subsequently received encouraging news about the injury , with NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reporting that Surtain's Achilles tendon was intact. Surtain missed Denver's 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 11 and its 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 15. The Broncos have relied on their depth in the secondary during his absence. Denver previously elevated two cornerbacks from its practice squad after injuries sidelined Surtain and fellow starter Riley Moss. Moss, who suffered a rib injury against San Francisco, returned against Seattle and played 20 defensive snaps. He practiced fully throughout this week and carries no injury designation for Sunday's game, giving Denver an important boost even if Surtain remains sidelined. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have also taken on larger responsibilities in the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian has continued handling the slot cornerback position. Denver's defensive depth remains under pressure elsewhere. The Broncos enter Sunday's matchup at 4-2 after consecutive victories, while the Cardinals are 2-4.

Surtain, who has missed Denver's last two games with an ankle injury, is unlikely to play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The update comes after Surtain returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering a non-contact ankle injury during Denver's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 4. The injury initially raised significant concerns because Surtain went down without contact late in the first half against San Francisco. However, the Broncos subsequently received encouraging news about the injury , with NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reporting that Surtain's Achilles tendon was intact. Surtain missed Denver's 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 11 and its 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 15. The Broncos have relied on their depth in the secondary during his absence. Denver previously elevated two cornerbacks from its practice squad after injuries sidelined Surtain and fellow starter Riley Moss. Moss, who suffered a rib injury against San Francisco, returned against Seattle and played 20 defensive snaps. He practiced fully throughout this week and carries no injury designation for Sunday's game, giving Denver an important boost even if Surtain remains sidelined. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have also taken on larger responsibilities in the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian has continued handling the slot cornerback position. Denver's defensive depth remains under pressure elsewhere. The Broncos enter Sunday's matchup at 4-2 after consecutive victories, while the Cardinals are 2-4.

Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. However, the Packers aren't going to be operating with a fully healthy offensive line going forward this season. It's been a banged-up unit this year already, and now, the Packers are losing another key starter. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Packers got some bad news on center Sean Rhyan, who is now set to miss multiple weeks as he deals with a high ankle sprain. Packers get bad news on Sean Rhyan amid high ankle sprain injury "Packers C Sean Rhyan, who left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, is believed to have suffered a high-ankle sprain, sources say," Rapoport reports. "X-Rays were negative, and he has an MRI today. But high-ankle sprains are often 4-6 week injuries." The Packers have already been dealing with some backups along the offensive line this season, and now, coming off a heartbreaking Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions , they just lost another key lineman. Now at 4-3, the Packers will be without Rhyan for multiple weeks, with this injury potentially one that lands him on injured reserve. In Week 8, the Packers will have to find a new center to play on Thursday Night Football against the Carolina Panthers . While the Panthers' defense isn't one to fear, this Packers team will need to fix this center problem in just a couple of days. Matt LaFleur has dealt with a ton of adversity this season, especially along the offensive line. This is another brutal blow, as the Packers OL struggles continue, with Rhyan's multi-week injury setting the team back once again. away.headline: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team's Week 7 loss to Lions
away.blurb: ・ Josh Jacobs says he is remorseful in first comments since Packers return The Green Bay Packers fell to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon by the score of 20-17. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials For their part, the Packers players themselves are not making excuses for the loss. That is, they are not at all saying that the reason they lost in Detroit was because of the officials. However, they are frustrated with the confusing calls made against them. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. away.headline: Green Bay Packers Slammed With Even More Bad Injury News
away.blurb: Starting center Sean Rhyan exited early in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return, forcing the Packers to scramble for interior protection against a physical Detroit front. Monk, who entered after Rhyan, also left early with a quadriceps issue and did not return, pushing John Williams—listed deeper on the depth chart and more accustomed to tackle duties—into emergency center snaps. With limited practice time and Rhyan unlikely to be available, the coaching staff must decide whether Monk can rebound quickly enough or if Williams will be asked to handle the bulk of the work. Green Bay Packers Slammed With Even More Bad Injury News - Packers Coverage Packers Coverage In-Depth Coverage of the Green Bay Packers [ October 26, 2026 ] Green Bay Packers Slammed With Even More Bad Injury News Packers [ October 26, 2026 ] Packers Star Puts NFL Officials on Blast After Controversial Loss Packers [ October 25, 2026 ] Packers' Micah Parsons Now Facing Potential NFL Punishment Packers [ October 25, 2026 ] Packers Get Sudden Update on Potential Jonathan Taylor Trade Packers [ October 24, 2026 ] Packers Make Massive Josh Jacobs Announcement Before Lions Game Packers The Green Bay Packers' offensive line took another significant hit during Sunday’s 20-17 defeat to the Detroit Lions. Initial evaluations pointed to a high ankle sprain. X-rays came back negative, and Rhyan was scheduled for an MRI the following day. Ian Rapoport of NFL media indicated the injury is expected to sideline him for four to six weeks, a typical recovery window for this type of sprain. High ankle sprains involve the ligaments connecting the tibia and fibula above the joint, often resulting from a planted foot being driven backward or rotated—precisely the mechanism described on the play when Rhyan went down. Rhyan had emerged as a stabilizing force along the line this season. The former UCLA standout and 2022 third-round pick transitioned from guard to center and started every game before the injury. His consistency mattered because the unit around him had already absorbed losses: other projected starters and key backups, including Jacob Monk, had missed time or dealt with their own ailments. The timing is especially difficult. Green Bay faces a short week with a Thursday night game against the Carolina Panthers in Week 8. Placing Rhyan on injured reserve remains a possibility if the MRI confirms the expected timeline, which would further thin an already depleted group. The Packers had begun to settle the line in recent weeks, but the combination of Rhyan’s absence and the earlier attrition leaves little margin for error. Centers must deliver both physicality in the run game and clean exchanges in the shotgun; any drop-off there can cascade into protection issues for the quarterback and reduced efficiency on the ground. Green Bay’s staff will spend the next few days sorting through internal options and monitoring recovery updates, knowing the next opponent arrives quickly

away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Both were estimated limited participants as Green Bay conducted a walkthrough rather than a full practice. The team's injury concerns extend beyond those two receivers, however. Love was also listed as limited Wednesday because of a back injury, while fellow wideout Savion Williams appeared with an ankle injury. The importance of having both receivers available becomes even clearer when considering what Detroit is preparing to defend. There's also the potential return of running back Josh Jacobs , who resumed practicing this week after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. With the Packers visiting Detroit at Ford Field on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, LaFleur's latest update suggests Green Bay should have its top two passing-game weapons available for a pivotal divisional matchup. home.headline: Jordan Love, Christian Watson among Packers off injury report and set to play vs. Lions
home.blurb: Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Savion Williams (ankle), and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are also off the injury report and are all set to play, despite being listed as limited all week. Guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), receiver Bo Melton (back), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jordan Riley (Achilles) are all questionable. Head coach Matt LaFleur noted earlier on Friday that linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) is out after suffering an injury on Thursday . home.headline: Lions, Packers Week 7 injury report: Bye week helps Detroit get healthy
home.blurb: C Cade Mays (Wrist, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week S Brian Branch (Achilles, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week On Monday, coach Dan Campbell told the media that the plan was to activate both Mays and Branch to the 53-man roster this week, but it was unclear how much either could play against the Packers. Branch is expected to “handle quite a bit,” but he may not be able to play the entire game, while Mays is expected to start based on Campbell’s comments on Wednesday : “We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — expected to return to play this season Branch’s safety running mate, Kerby Joseph, also got some positive news this week, as Campbell noted on Tuesday that he still expects the All-Pro safety to return to play this season. While there is still no timetable for his return, this was the first positive update we have gotten from coaches surrounding Joseph’s status and was quickly followed up by even more promising videos posted on Joseph’s social media accounts . Ya-Sin was injured on special teams in Week 4, missed the Lions game in Week 5, but was able to get healthy enough to practice over the bye and was back on the practice field on Tuesday. While he’s no longer in the starting lineup on defense, he’s been a steady contributor on multiple phases of special teams and would boost multiple spots if he could return to game action. C Cade Mays (Wrist) — Upgraded from limited practice S Brian Branch (Achilles) — Upgraded from limited practice As mentioned above, Mays and Branch are on track to return and start this week. Williams was limited in practice in Week 5 but was able to play a full complement of snaps in the game and looked like the injury didn’t limit him. Wonnum also managed to play in Week 5 (50% of defensive snaps), but it’s unclear if his snaps were scaled back a tick due to injury or schematic approach. It didn’t look like his injury limited him too much, considering he registered another two sacks in the game.
