picks.blurb: Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game Marvin Uzor, Raiders Wire Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:50 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week, Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr was nearly the sole holdout in picking the Raiders to edge past the Buffalo Bills . Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.headline: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday’s practice. That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury’s severity or confirm he will miss kickoff. His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active. The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere. Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams’ absence reduces its options, and Nacua’s availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Seahawks: NFL Week 7 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Kansas City Chiefs are back in prime time this weekend, taking center stage at Lumen Field in a matter of hours against a feisty Seattle Seahawks squad that's still finding its way a bit after winning the Super Bowl earlier this calendar year. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. If Mahomes starts finding his receivers, the box opens up for Walker. At some point, one of those two is going to win. On the other side, if Sam Darnold can buy time in the pocket, Smith-Njigba is going to get loose. The Chiefs’ defense just has to make sure that happens once or twice rather than repeatedly. They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. Chiefs at Seahawks SNF: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction This is technically the second meeting between these two teams this year, following an ugly preseason tie in August that featured mostly second and third-string players. While Seattle boasts one of the best home-field advantages in the sport, the matchup predictor still gives the undefeated Chiefs a slight edge to maintain their perfect record. Chiefs on SI's Take Usually, the matchup predictor closely mirrors what traditional betting lines are forecasting. However, that isn't the case for this contest. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. Unlike some of their past opponents, Patrick Mahomes will make them pay. away.headline: Chiefs Cool Hill Reunion: Andy Reid says nothing is happening; injury timeline clouds return
away.source: The Times of India on MSN
away.blurb: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Kansas City Chiefs has hit a significant roadblock, leaving fans wondering whether the explosive wide receiver will wear the red and gold again. What once looked like a promising reunion has lost momentum as concerns over his recovery continue to shape the conversation. With the Chiefs winning games and Patrick Mahomes leading the offence, Kansas City faces a difficult choice: take a chance on a familiar star or trust the players already on the roster. For Hill, the bigger challenge remains proving he can return to the field at his best. Without a clear medical assessment and a confirmed return timeline, Kansas City may be unwilling to take that risk. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Why the Chiefs are hesitant to sign Tyreek Hill However, Hill’s health remains the biggest obstacle. The 32-year-old suffered a dislocated left knee and multiple ligament tears while playing for the Miami Dolphins during Week 4 of the 2025 NFL season. His injury required two surgeries, making his road back to professional football particularly challenging. Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has offered encouraging updates about his client’s rehabilitation and readiness to explore opportunities with NFL teams. Yet positive training reports cannot replace the medical assessments teams need before committing to a player recovering from such a serious injury. Hill built his reputation on elite speed, sharp changes of direction and the ability to turn short passes into game-changing plays. Those qualities make him dangerous, but they also raise questions about how quickly he can regain his previous form. Andy Reid’s Tyreek Hill update offers little hope of a reunion The comments suggest Kansas City is not preparing to rush into a deal, despite the team's earlier need for additional receiving options. Mahomes has also given the Chiefs reason to remain patient. He has started the 2026 campaign strongly, distributing the ball to targets such as Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. That production gives the coaching staff less reason to disrupt its current offensive plans for a player whose availability remains uncertain. Roster planning is another consideration. Bringing Hill back would require the team to assess his conditioning, recovery progress and ability to handle the demands of an NFL season. Promoting players who already understand Reid’s system could offer a more straightforward solution. Still, the situation could change if Kansas City suffers more injuries or Hill receives medical clearance sooner than expected. For now, Hill remains a free agent, and the Chiefs appear content to move forward without him. A reunion is not impossible, but the former Kansas City star must first overcome the uncertainty surrounding his recovery before any serious move becomes realistic. away.blurb: The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve Thursday. The earliest he can return is Nov. 22 for Kansas City's Week 11 contest against the Arizona Cardinals. Simmons played in eight of 17 games last season. He was out from Weeks 6-9 due to personal reasons involving his family. The 23-year-old returned for two games before suffering a dislocated and broken wrist against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals KANSAS CITY CHIEFS Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes asked Chiefs lineman to leave team meeting: Report Chris Bumbaca USA TODAY Updated Oct. 25, 2026, 7:34 p.m. CT The Kansas City Chiefs enter their Week 7 "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Seattle Seahawks undefeated. But not all is cheery for the 5-0 squad, with starting left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve for a lingering back injury and an NFL Network report that the 2025 first-round pick was asked to leave a team meeting by head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes. According to the report, Simmons – who has not yet appeared in a game this season – was sitting with his feet up during an offensive team meeting. Reid asked him to put his feet down, per the report, and Simmons replied that he had to sit in that manner because of back discomfort. Reid then told Simmons to seek treatment if he was in pain, according to witnesses cited in the NFL Network report, and when Simmons protested more, Mahomes also spoke up. Simmons later apologized to Reid and team leaders, per NFL Network. He was placed on injured reserve Thursday, Oct. 22, with Chiefs vice president of sports medicine and performance and head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder telling reporters that Simmons attempted to rehab a herniated, bulging disk in his lumbar spine – which caused the calf discomfort he felt during camp – before a lack of progress encouraged the medical team to shut him down again. The Chiefs have deployed undrafted rookie Khalil Benson at left tackle in Simmons' absence. If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission. away.headline: ‘They have been calling around' - NFL Insider gives latest updates on Kansas City Chiefs' trade pursuits ahead of November's deadline
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs are working the phones after injuries depleted their wide receiver room, ESPN’s Adam Schefter says. Here’s a look at the trade targets who could be available and the one who truly stands out. “I think the bigger issue last night, we talked about on Get Up this morning, was the offensive tackle position. They had two new offensive tackles in last night, couldn’t keep the defense away from Patrick Mahomes. Couldn’t mount the ground game that they have in other years, and they kind of feed off each other. Right, if the protection’s coming, then the run game’s thriving, and just none of that worked last night. Then they didn’t reach the red zone a single time for the first time in Patrick Mahomes’ NFL career. So, I think it was just all out of whack. Several names stand out as potential trade candidates, though each one comes with a catch. Eagles WR Marquise Brown: Brown is also being floated as an option. He already has familiarity with the Chiefs’ system, but he had limited success during his previous stint with the team. This wouldn’t be an upgrade. Instead, it would be a desperate attempt to find some consistency with a player who knows the offense and could integrate quickly. Only one option in that category may be available: Jets WR Garrett Wilson. With a strong enough return, Wilson could be pried away, like any player. As far as difference-making players go, he’s probably the only one who fits what the Chiefs truly lack at the position. Whether Kansas City is willing to pay that price, and whether the Jets are willing to listen, remains to be seen. The Kansas City Chiefs have a wide receiver problem. Injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice have depleted the position group, and it showed in Week 7’s game against the Seattle Seahawks. Kansas City’s top wide receiver, rookie Cyrus Allen, finished with just 18 yards on one catch. The rest of the group made so little impact that Mike Tirico couldn’t even get their names right . Now, the Chiefs are looking for outside help ahead of the NFL trade deadline . Whether they find it is another matter. away.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . It has been a brutally tough season for both teams, with Philly and Dallas both sitting at 2-4 entering Week 7. The Cowboys and Eagles were viewed as the best teams in the division going into the season, yet they are both trailing the New York Giants, who look like the least dysfunctional team in the NFC East after seven weeks. But all that matters right now is what happens on Monday night. And, speaking of Monday night, here's a look at who the majority of experts from different media outlets are picking between the Cowboys and Eagles. Mandatory Credit: Ross Harried-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowboys: 27 This is absolutely a game the Cowboys should win going away, even though it's a road contest against a hated division rival. After all, the Eagles won't have Jalen Hurts and are instead starting Tanner McKee, and even their best wide receiver, Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith, are out . Philly is going to be short-handed on defense, also, with Nolan Smith, who is their sacks leader, ruled out, and then there's also Jonathan Greenard, who is questionable to play . However, after what we've witnessed over the last six weeks, there are no guarantees with this lackluster Cowboys team, and especially because of the putrid defense . There is hope yet, though, as the defense will welcome back Cobie Durant, who was the Cowboys' best corner during the offseason, and DeMarvion Overshown. The returns of those two players , combined with the Eagles' key injuries on offense, should be enough for the Cowboys to have a bounce-back showing on defense and keep Philly in check. On offense, Dallas has struggled the past two games , but this is also a good bounce-back spot for the unit, as Philly's pass defense has been very disappointing this season. We're still very leery of the clear trap game this is, but we are going to go out on a limb and say the Cowboys take care of business against the Eagles on Monday night. If not, the Cowboys should leave Brian Schottenheimer in Philly. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
